Sensitivity Analysis for Sample Size Planning From the AIPE Perspective for a Mean Under Two-Phase Sampling

Source: R/ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity.R
ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity.Rd

Evaluates a two-phase design by simulation: how wide the confidence intervals from ci_two_phase turn out to be, how often they are no wider than planned, and how often they miss the population mean of the target, when the design is carried out in a population that may differ from the one the plan assumed. The design is either planned by ss_aipe_two_phase from planning values, so that the distance between planning values and population values is what is studied, or fixed by the user.

Usage

ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity(
  true_sd_Y = NULL,
  true_cor = NULL,
  supposed_sd_Y = NULL,
  supposed_cor = NULL,
  specified_n_labeled = NULL,
  n_pool,
  width,
  population = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  assurance = NULL,
  true_kurtosis = 0,
  G = 1000,
  print_iter = FALSE,
  filename = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

true_sd_Y, true_cor

The population standard deviation of the target measurement and its correlation with the proxy, from which the data are generated when population is NULL.

supposed_sd_Y, supposed_cor

Planning values passed to ss_aipe_two_phase to choose the number of labeled units; supply both, or specified_n_labeled instead.

specified_n_labeled

The number of labeled units to evaluate, in place of a planned one.

n_pool

The number of units in the pool, \(M\), a whole number larger than the number of labeled units.

width

The desired full width of the confidence interval, the planning target and the yardstick for pct_ci_less_width.

population

NULL (default) for a bivariate normal population, or a data frame of observed (target, proxy) pairs with numeric columns y and x, to be resampled with replacement as the population; true_sd_Y and true_cor are then computed from it and must not be supplied.

conf_level

Confidence level (default 0.95).

assurance, true_kurtosis

Passed to ss_aipe_two_phase when the design is planned; see that page.

G

The number of Monte Carlo replications (default 1000).

print_iter

Logical; print the replication number as the loop runs.

filename

Optional path for a comma separated file recording every replication (the estimate mean_Y, the two confidence limits, the interval width, and two indicators of whether the interval missed the population mean below or above): nothing is written when filename is NULL (the default), a new file with a header row is created otherwise, an existing file at that path is appended to, and a throwaway run should point it at tempfile(fileext = ".csv").

seed

NULL (default) to draw from the current random number stream, or a number that makes the run reproducible without disturbing the stream of the calling script.

Value

A data.frame (class dmar_tbl) with term and value columns: mean_mean_Y, median_mean_Y, and sd_mean_Y for the estimates of the target mean; the realized widths (mean_ci_width, median_ci_width, sd_ci_width); the proportion of intervals no wider than width (pct_ci_less_width); the proportions that missed the population mean from above (pct_ci_miss_low, the mean below the lower limit) and from below (pct_ci_miss_high) and their sum (total_type_I_error), all on the 0 to 1 scale; then n_labeled, total_N (the pool size \(M\), the design's total number of units, which the rest of the two-phase family calls n_pool; the sensitivity family's shared schema names the size of a whole design total_N), true_mean_Y (the population target mean), true_sd_Y, true_cor, supposed_sd_Y and supposed_cor (NA when specified_n_labeled was given), width, conf_level, and, only when one was supplied, assurance and true_kurtosis. The number of replications used is in the simulation attribute (its element returned), described below.

Details

The data generating mechanism. With population = NULL, each replication draws the \(n\) labeled units as (target, proxy) pairs from a bivariate normal distribution with standard deviations true_sd_Y and 1, correlation true_cor, and means 0, and the \(M - n\) unlabeled units' proxies from the same proxy distribution. The interval's width and coverage do not depend on the two means or on the proxy's scale, so these choices lose no generality; the population target mean the intervals are scored against is then 0. Because the regression estimator uses the unlabeled proxies only through their mean and their sum of squares, the simulation draws those two from their exact joint distribution (independent normal and scaled chi square) rather than drawing every unit of the pool, which keeps a large pool cheap. With a population data frame, each replication resamples the labeled pairs and the unlabeled proxies with replacement from its rows, a population that keeps whatever skew, bounds, or nonlinearity the observed pairs have; the target mean scored against is then the mean of its y column. In the evaluation of a system whose outputs an automated judge labels, for example, a pilot set of outputs carrying both a human assessor's label and the judge's makes such a population.

What is evaluated. Each replication computes the regression interval of ci_two_phase (the interval the planner plans for) and records its width and whether it missed the population target mean below or above. A replication whose labeled units all share one proxy value has no regression interval, and one whose labeled units all share one target value would have an interval of zero width, which ci_two_phase refuses. Either can happen only with a population data frame, chiefly one whose proxy takes few distinct values or whose target is binary with a proportion near 0 or 1. Such replications are dropped, with a single warning that counts each kind, and the number kept is attr(x, "simulation")$returned (see the section on the record of the simulation). Many dropped replications say that the design has too few labeled units for that population, and the summaries, which describe the replications that produced an interval, then flatter the design.

The record of the simulation

Every sensitivity function of the package summarizes its replications over one denominator: the replications that produced a confidence interval (for a power sensitivity function, a test). The proportion of intervals that met the width target (pct_ci_less_width), the proportions of intervals that missed the true value, and the summaries of the widths are all taken over those replications. A replication without an interval is in none of these rows. It is counted, and the returned table carries the counts in its attribute simulation, a list read with attr(x, "simulation"):

attempted

the number of replications asked for (G).

returned

the number that produced an interval (a test).

failed

the number that did not (attempted - returned).

denominator

the number of replications the rows named above are taken over, which is returned.

width_target_probability

the proportion of the replications with an interval whose interval met the width target, the value of the pct_ci_less_width row; NA for a function or a call without a width target, and when no replication produced an interval.

width_target_mc_ci

the exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) limits for that proportion, at the confidence level of the table. They describe the error of the simulation, which shrinks as G grows, and nothing else.

A function that records more about its run adds elements to the list, and its help page names them. The line "Replications" beneath the printed table gives G, and the three counts when a replication was without an interval. With many replications without an interval the rows describe only the studies in which the interval could be formed, so failed is to be reported beside them.

References

Kelley, K., & Rausch, J. R. (2006). Sample size planning for the standardized mean difference: Accuracy in parameter estimation via narrow confidence intervals. Psychological Methods, 11(4), 363–385. doi:10.1037/1082-989X.11.4.363

Neyman, J. (1938). Contribution to the theory of sampling human populations. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 33(201), 101–116. doi:10.1080/01621459.1938.10503378

Examples

# A plan made with a correlation of 0.55, carried out where the
# correlation is only 0.45. G = 200 keeps the example quick; a reported
# evaluation deserves the default G = 1000 or more.
ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity(true_sd_Y = 0.43, true_cor = 0.45,
                              supposed_sd_Y = 0.43, supposed_cor = 0.55,
                              n_pool = 20000, width = 0.10,
                              conf_level = 0.90, G = 200, seed = 113)
#>  term               value
#>  mean_mean_Y        0.000
#>  median_mean_Y      0.001
#>  sd_mean_Y          0.032
#>  mean_ci_width      0.107
#>  median_ci_width    0.106
#>  sd_ci_width        0.007
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.180
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.045
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.060
#>  total_type_I_error 0.105
#>  n_labeled          142  
#>  total_N            20000
#>  true_mean_Y        0    
#>  true_sd_Y          0.430
#>  true_cor           0.450
#>  supposed_sd_Y      0.430
#>  supposed_cor       0.550
#>  width              0.100
#>  conf_level         0.900
#> 
#> Replications: 200
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%

# A fixed design, 150 labeled units in a pool of 5,000, evaluated in a
# population of binary (target, proxy) pairs resampled from a pilot of
# 300 units: how often is the 90% interval narrower than 0.085?
set.seed(113)
proxy  <- rbinom(300, 1, 0.6)
target <- ifelse(runif(300) < 0.8, proxy, rbinom(300, 1, 0.6))
ss_aipe_two_phase_sensitivity(specified_n_labeled = 150, n_pool = 5000,
                              width = 0.085, conf_level = 0.90,
                              population = data.frame(y = target, x = proxy),
                              G = 200, seed = 113)
#>  term               value
#>  mean_mean_Y        0.565
#>  median_mean_Y      0.565
#>  sd_mean_Y          0.024
#>  mean_ci_width      0.084
#>  median_ci_width    0.084
#>  sd_ci_width        0.009
#>  pct_ci_less_width  0.520
#>  pct_ci_miss_low    0.035
#>  pct_ci_miss_high   0.035
#>  total_type_I_error 0.070
#>  n_labeled          150  
#>  total_N            5000 
#>  true_mean_Y        0.567
#>  true_sd_Y          0.496
#>  true_cor           0.789
#>  supposed_sd_Y      <NA> 
#>  supposed_cor       <NA> 
#>  width              0.085
#>  conf_level         0.900
#> 
#> Replications: 200
#> 
#> Confidence level: 90%
